query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for jet-turbine applications, what single intervention could improve high-temperature mechanical capability while limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its mechanism, the expected improvement relative to a relevant baseline, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive experiment with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small amount (about 0.5 at%) of carbon into a NbMoTaW high-entropy alloy will form stable MC-type carbide precipitates that improve high-temperature strength by ~10–15% relative to the undoped alloy, while keeping density below ~11 g·cm⁻³ and preserving room-temperature ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: A NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (four principal elements) with an equiatomic or near-equiatomic composition.
generation.intervention: Add 0.5 at% C (carbon) to the alloy melt before casting/solidification.
generation.conditions: Thermomechanical testing at temperatures up to 1200 °C under compressive loading; room-temperature mechanical testing for ductility checks.
generation.structural_mediator: Fine, stable MC-type carbide precipitates dispersed at grain boundaries and in the matrix.
generation.mechanism: The carbide precipitates act as pinning sites countering dislocation motion and limiting grain-boundary sliding at high temperatures, thereby improving high-temperature mechanical capability.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the undoped alloy, the C-doped material will demonstrate ~10–15% higher yield strength at 1200 °C, similar density (≤11 g·cm⁻³), and comparable ductility at room temperature.
generation.baseline: An identical alloy composition without carbon addition, tested under the same thermal and mechanical conditions.
generation.boundary: At higher carbon concentrations than 0.5 at%, excessive carbide formation may increase brittleness or degrade room-temperature ductility.
generation.uncertainty: If carbide precipitation is not uniform or if carbides coarsen prematurely, the strengthening effect may be diminished; this remains to be confirmed experimentally.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of NbMoTaW alloy specimens, one doped with 0.5 at% C and one undoped. Homogenize, then subject both batches to identical thermomechanical treatments. Measure density, perform tensile tests at room temperature, and compression tests at 1200 °C to compare yield strength and ductility.
measurements: Density measurements to ensure values remain below ~11 g·cm⁻³
Microstructural characterization (SEM/TEM) to confirm carbide formation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the doped alloy does not show higher yield strength at 1200 °C, or if its density exceeds ~11 g·cm⁻³, or if its room-temperature ductility is significantly compromised relative to the baseline alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.
